messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed the prefix cache token-saved metric dropped ~60% for a subset of customers after yesterday's batching tweak. Grafana panel shows hit_rate down for model:mistral-8k route:/chat and customer:acme-inc. anyone else seeing this?

aj: saw the spike in miss rate too. quick numbers from the query: 
```
# prometheus-ish
sum by(customer, route, model) (rate(prefix_cache_hits[5m])) / sum by(customer, route, model) (rate(prefix_cache_requests[5m]))
```
acme-inc hit_rate: 0.43 -> 0.16; overall global hit_rate: 0.71 -> 0.62

sam: hmm, batching heuristic change was supposed to only affect pack_size selection. Could it be key normalization timing? we changed canonicalization to be async on the request path.

maria: timeline — change rolled at 23:10 UTC, anomalies start ~23:12. matches.

aleo: (that's me) I pushed a small change to move key-hash to IO thread to reduce latency. I thought it preserved semantics.

leo: can we check example cache keys that missed vs hit? need to confirm if we introduced nondeterminism (whitespace/metadata ordering).

aj: grabbed a sample from logs: 
```
miss keys sample:
- "mistral-8k|/chat|cust:acme-inc|prompt_hash:ab12|seed:42"
- "mistral-8k|/chat|cust:acme-inc|prompt_hash:ab12|seed:0"
hit keys sample:
- "mistral-8k|/chat|cust:acme-inc|prompt_hash:ab12|seed:0"
```
looks like seed field is inconsistent for same client flows (we normalize seed only for cached completions, not streaming warmups).

anya: that would explain token-saved drop — many warmups now generate slightly different key due to nondet seed insertion. warmups were our primary source of prefix cache population for acme-inc.

ops-bot: Incident note — alert prefix_cache.hit_rate.customer.acme-inc crossed threshold (0.25) at 2026-03-16T23:12:45Z. Pager: none (informational).

maria: action plan: (1) lock down key canonicalization — remove volatile fields from cache key generation, (2) add unit test for deterministic keying, (3) add Grafana breakdown per-route/per-customer + example sample log link, (4) temporary mitigation: enable aggressive prefix warmup for acme-inc. assign owners?

leo: I can do (1) and (2) — will open a PR to move key construction to the synchronous path but keep it cheap. target in next 2 hours.

aj: I'll add the per-customer drilldown to the dashboard and add a token-saved column (tokens_saved = tokens_before - tokens_after from cached prefix use). simple PromQL: 
```
sum by(customer) (increase(prefix_tokens_saved[1h]))
```

sam: for (4) I can flip warmup-policy for acme-inc to "eager" for 24h so we rebuild cache while fix rolls out.

anya: we should also instrument a histogram of key-variance per-route: cardinality of distinct(cache_key_fingerprint) / total_requests to catch regressions early.

maria: agree. add alert: key_variance.customer > 0.05 triggers paging — that would catch changes like this earlier.

leo: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/p/runtime/pulls/482 — contains deterministic keying + tests. will watch CI.

aj: dashboard update pushed to grafana staging: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/prefix-cache/prefix-cache-overview (added per-model/per-route/per-customer panels + tokens_saved table). please review.

ops-bot: CI: runtime/unit-tests passed for PR 482.

maria: rolling the eager warmup for acme-inc now (api flag). i'll monitor token-saved metric; if it recovers to previous level within 30m we can keep eager for 24h then revert.

sam: warmup toggled -> api call: `POST /admin/warmup?customer=acme-inc&policy=eager` returned 200.

(30 minutes later)

maria: quick update — hit_rate for acme-inc back to 0.68 after warmup + PR merged. tokens_saved recovered to ~92% of pre-incident baseline. closing loop: key variance alert added on staging.

leo: follow-ups: add synthetic nightly prewarm job for high-commit customers; document cache key schema in docs repo.

maria: thanks all. we'll keep dashboard alerting and add regression test in the perf suite to catch future keying churn. :thumbsup:
